question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

choices.text: it was Lise Meitner's experimental notes that went on
Lise Meitner's experimental notes went on
the experimental notes belonging to Lise Meitner went on

explanation: The correct answer is B, "Lise Meitner went on." The introductory phrase "Trained as a physicist in Berlin and forced to leave Germany in 1938" must modify the subject of the main clause, and only a person can be trained as a physicist and forced to leave Germany. "Lise Meitner went on to use her experimental notes … to recognize … that the barium Hahn had detected … was a sign of nuclear fission" places that person in the subject position, so the modifier attaches correctly. The other options make "experimental notes" the subject — directly in C and D, and through a cleft construction in A — leaving the introductory phrase dangling, since notes cannot be trained or forced to flee.

_meta.anchor: Lise Meitner — physicist; fled Nazi Germany 1938; nuclear fission (Dec. 1938); dangling modifier

passage: Trained as a physicist in Berlin and forced to leave Germany in 1938, ______ to use her experimental notes — sent to Sweden ahead of her — to recognize, in correspondence with Otto Hahn that December, that the barium Hahn had detected after bombarding uranium with neutrons was a sign of nuclear fission.
